author: Rolly Gacelo
title: Knicks Coach Mike Brown Gets 1st Technical Foul of the Season, Gives Backhanded Compliment to SGA - NewsBreak
text:
By Rolly Gacelo ,
1 hours ago Mike Brown is not the type to easily get riled up, but on Wednesday he got heated enough to earn his first technical foul of the season. His New York Knicks were in a close matchup against Western Conference giants the Oklahoma City Thunder , and with the way it ended, every call mattered.
The play that led to Brown’s technical foul involved Thunder star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Jalen Brunson. Gilgeous-Alexander has been critiqued many times for foul-baiting, and the Knicks experienced it firsthand.
SGA would have picked up his third foul on that play, and it was still just the first quarter.
Brown explained his reaction after the game.
“You guys saw the play. SGA had two fouls and Jalen was there and he ran him over, just like the call they made on OG,” he told reporters.
“I don’t understand why that was a no-call but that should’ve been his third.”
The Knicks lost the game , 100-103.
Oklahoma City Thunder star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander goes for the lay-up versus Knicks
Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Mike Brown ‘compliments’ SGA SGA went on to punish the Knicks and finished the game with 26 points and eight assists. Chet Holmgren led the Thunder with 28 points.
Brown said they had a hard time containing the 2025 MVP, calling him a tough cover. The two-time Coach of the Year praised the Canadian, though not without a bit of shade .
“SGA, he’s a tough cover. He does a great job of convincing the referees – probably better than anybody in the league – that he’s getting hit,” he told reporters after the game.
“Then he shoot 84 percent from the free throw line compared to our 73 percent. It was factor throughout the course of the game.”
